meanings.note: Usually preceded by يوم (day) or definite الأحد in Jordanian schedules.

examples.text: يوم الأحد الصبح بنفتح المكتبة بدري.
examples.trans: On Sunday morning we open the library early.

examples.text: رح نتجمع كلنا بالحديقة يوم أحد هادي.
examples.trans: We will all gather in the park on a quiet Sunday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: I bought four books.
The guests arrived at four in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite having no -a ending; means ground, land, or indoor floor.

examples.trans: The floor is clean and dry now.
Set the box on the floor for a moment.

أصلا.gloss: anyway; in the first place; actually

meanings.en: anyway; in the first place; actually
meanings.note: Everyday conversational adverb meaning 'in the first place / anyway / to begin with'.

examples.trans: Does the attic even have a comfortable bed?
The wire needed adjusting anyway.

meanings.note: Used to express certainty or agreement.

examples.trans: I will certainly come to the party.

examples.text: أكيد ما رح أنسى أجبلك الكتاب بكرة الصبح.
examples.trans: For sure I won't forget to bring you the book tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Relational adjective from أمام ('in front of'): الغرفة الأمامية / الباب الأمامي.

examples.text: علقنا اللوحة الجديدة جنب البوابة الأمامية.
examples.trans: We hung the new sign beside the front gate.
The front windows look straight out onto the lane.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) of Form IV أعار; used in library phrases like رف الإعارة.

examples.text: هادا الكتاب موجود على رف الإعارة بالمكتبة.
examples.trans: This book is on the lending shelf in the library.
The loan period for the novel is only two weeks.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: Precious metal, culturally significant for weddings in Jordan.

examples.trans: They bought the gold for my brother's engagement.

examples.text: أسعار الذهب طلعت هالأيام بسوق الصاغة.
examples.trans: Gold prices went up these days in the goldsmiths' market.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Used to describe colors that have lost their brightness or people looking pale.

examples.text: لون القميص صار باهت من الغسيل.
examples.trans: The shirt's color became faded from washing.
The book cover has a faded green colour.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: A highly versatile prefix used as a preposition of place or instrument.

examples.trans: We went to work by car.

examples.text: اكتب اسمك بـ قلم الحبر على البطاقة.
examples.trans: Write your name with the fountain pen on the card.

meanings.note: Used to refer to something made of or covered with fabric.

examples.trans: He covered the table with a red cloth.

examples.text: غطينا سلة الخبز بقماش كتان أبيض.
examples.trans: We covered the bread basket with white linen cloth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: I have nine books on the shelf.

examples.text: الساعة تسعة الصبح رح نلتقي عند النافورة.
examples.trans: At nine in the morning we will meet by the fountain.

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: His age is now thirty years.

examples.text: ضلينا تلاتين دقيقة بنستنى الكيكة تبرد.
examples.trans: We spent thirty minutes waiting for the cake to cool.

meanings.note: Form V verb from نفس ('breath').

examples.text: فتحت الشباك عشان أتنفس هوا نضيف.
examples.trans: I opened the window to breathe fresh air.

examples.text: بعد ما رتبنا القائمة، قدرت أتنفس براحة.
examples.trans: Once we organized the list, I could breathe easily.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجراس.

examples.trans: The gate bell rang twice.
Listen to the sound of the bell in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Go inside the house, the weather is cold.
The metal tin is hidden inside the cupboard.

meanings.note: With possessive endings, حال acts as 'myself/yourself/itself' (لحاله by itself, لا تغلبي حالك don't tire yourself).

examples.trans: The door opened by itself from the wind.
How are you doing today?

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Is anyone here?

examples.text: في حدا بعرف وين نحفظت الخريطة؟
examples.trans: Does anyone know where the map was stored?

meanings.note: Standard and Jordanian feminine noun for a public park or walled garden (حدائق 'parks').

examples.trans: The park bench is painted beside the arch.

examples.text: بنتمشى بالحديقة كل يوم جمعة العصر.
examples.trans: We walk in the park every Friday afternoon.

meanings.note: Polite traditional title of respect for a woman in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لو الجرس رن مرة واحدة يا خانوم كنت استغربت.
examples.trans: If the bell rang only once, madam, I would be surprised.

examples.text: تفضلي الكرسي هادا يا خانوم سعاد.
examples.trans: Please take this chair, Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian adjective for broken machines, bells, or spoiled food.

examples.text: الجرس ما برن منيح، أكيد السلك خربان.
examples.trans: The bell is not ringing properly; the wire must be broken.
The old clock has been out of order for two years.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of دائما ('always').

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.
Noon traffic is always slow.

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Can mean the metal lead, or bullets. Often used in 'qalam rSaaS' (pencil).

examples.trans: Write with a pencil so you can erase it.

examples.text: الرقم مكتوب بقلم رصاص خفيف جنب الزاوية.
examples.trans: The number is written in light pencil near the corner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: رفوف.

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
There are two pieces left on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: What is your phone number?

examples.text: كل بطاقة إلها رقم متسلسل من واحد لعشرة.
examples.trans: Each card has a serial number from one to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برن, بيرن).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
The old wire always rings twice.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رنّ (to ring).

examples.text: هاد الرنين المزدوج أكيد من غرفة أربعة.
examples.trans: That double ringing is definitely from Room Four.

examples.text: سمعنا رنين الجرس من آخر الساحة.
examples.trans: We heard the ringing of the bell from the far end of the courtyard.

meanings.note: Verb رنّ means 'to ring' (for a bell, phone, or timer).

examples.text: المنبّه رنّ الساعة ستة بس ما قمت علطول.
examples.trans: The alarm rang at six, but I didn't get up right away.

examples.text: جرس الباب عم برنّ، شكله الضيوف وصلوا.
examples.trans: The doorbell is ringing; looks like the guests have arrived.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: Put the chair in the corner.
The chest is placed in the northern corner of the room.

meanings.note: Singular noun of unity with ta marbuta; collective noun is زهر (flowers). Also used for cauliflower in Levantine food contexts.

examples.text: في زهرة بيضا مرسومة على غلاف الكتاب.
examples.trans: There is a white flower drawn on the cover of the book.
The garden is full of colourful blossoms in spring.

meanings.note: Ordinal adjective on the faa'il pattern corresponding to سبعة (seven); inflects for feminine سابعة.

examples.text: المخبز القديم موجود بالشارع السابع عاليمين.
examples.trans: The old bakery is on the seventh street on the right.

examples.text: هاي المرة السابعة اللي بنعد فيها الخطوات.
examples.trans: This is the seventh time we count the steps.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسلاك.

examples.trans: The old wire needs a slight adjustment.
We checked the bell wire by the door.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: This car is this year's model.

examples.text: مرّت سنة كاملة على آخر زيارة للمزرعة.
examples.trans: A whole year has passed since the last visit to the farm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Very common adverb in Jordanian Arabic for 'a little bit' or 'slowly'.

examples.text: امشي شوي شوي عشان ما توقع.
examples.trans: Walk slowly so you don't fall.

examples.text: استنوا شوي عشان تبرد الصواني تماما.
examples.trans: Wait a little so the trays cool down completely.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

meanings.note: The season of summer.

examples.trans: Summer in Jordan is usually hot.

examples.text: بالصيف بنحب نقعد بالعريشة تحت العنب.
examples.trans: In the summer we like to sit under the grape arbour.

meanings.note: Onomatopoeic verbal noun describing the buzz of bees or a steady ringing hum.

examples.text: سمعنا طنين النحل حوالين شجر اللوز.
examples.trans: We heard the buzzing of bees around the almond trees.

examples.text: طنين الساعة القديمة بنسمع من آخر الممر.
examples.trans: The humming of the old clock can be heard from the end of the hall.

meanings.note: Used for giving directions (straight ahead) or referring to time (immediately).

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead then turn right.

examples.text: روح طوالي لآخر الممر وبتلاقي المكتبة.
examples.trans: Go straight ahead to the end of the corridor and you will find the library.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عادات.

examples.trans: Usually we open the gate at seven.
Drinking morning coffee is a nice habit.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: I went to the doctor because I am sick.

examples.text: استعملنا ورق نشافة عشان الحبر ما يطبع.
examples.trans: We used blotting paper so the ink would not stain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أعشاب.

examples.trans: We sprinkled green herbs on top of the eggs.
Tariq grows fresh herbs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Arabic distinguishes father's sister (عمة, feminine of عمّ) from mother's sister (خالة).

examples.text: عمتي كانت تعزف عالبيانو كل يوم جمعة.
examples.trans: My paternal aunt used to play the piano every Friday.

examples.text: هاد الدفتر الأخضر هدية من عمتي.
examples.trans: This green notebook is a gift from my aunt.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: The bedroom is very spacious.

examples.text: غرفة المكتبة هادية ومليانة كتب خرائط.
examples.trans: The library room is quiet and full of atlases.

meanings.note: Refers to a book cover, box sleeve, or outer wrapping; plural أغلفة.

examples.text: غلاف الدفتر القديم لونه أزرق باهت.
examples.trans: The cover of the old notebook is a faded blue.

examples.text: حطينا غلاف شفاف عشان نحمي الخريطة.
examples.trans: We put a clear cover on to protect the map.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفحص, بيفحص).

examples.trans: Tariq will inspect the cellar right away.
We checked the heater and pipes this morning.

meanings.note: Polysemous noun used for a season of the year, a chapter in a book, or a school class; plural فصول.

examples.text: الأرز البري بنجمع بفصل الصيف عادة.
examples.trans: Wild rice is usually harvested in the summer season.

examples.text: اقرأ الفصل الأول من الدفتر قبل ما تكمل.
examples.trans: Read the first chapter of the notebook before continuing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفكر, بيفكر).

examples.trans: I thought it was lost when we sold the house!
We thought the matter through calmly.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The book is on top of the table.

examples.text: الخريطة معلقة فوق الرف الخشبي بالمكتبة.
examples.trans: The map is hanging above the wooden shelf in the library.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.trans: I have to arrive before five o'clock.

examples.text: غسلنا الفواكه منيح قبل ما نقطعها للتذوق.
examples.trans: We washed the fruit thoroughly before slicing it for the tasting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.trans: I will arrive very soon.

examples.text: سلمى رح ترجع قريب ومعها مرطبان العسل الجبلي.
examples.trans: Salma will be back soon bringing the jar of mountain honey.

meanings.note: With بـ + الـ, بالقوة means 'by force / forcefully'.

examples.trans: She grabbed my hand forcefully.
Honesty gives us strength.

meanings.note: Vocalized in the dictionary to distinguish Form I قَلَب ('to flip, turn a page over') from the noun قلب ('heart').

examples.text: اقلبي الصفحة وشوفي شو مكتوب وراها.
examples.trans: Turn the page over and see what is written on the back.

examples.text: قلب طارق الصندوق عشان يقرا الرقم تحت.
examples.trans: Tariq flipped the box over to read the number underneath.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: The weather was cold yesterday.

examples.text: الطعم كان متوازن كتير بين العسل والليمون.
examples.trans: The flavour was very well balanced between the honey and lemon.

meanings.note: The Amman verb for pressing a button, doorbell or switch.

examples.text: اكبس الزر الأحمر عشان يفتح الباب.
examples.trans: Press the red button to open the door.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرتين وما حدا فتح.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell twice and nobody opened.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.trans: He wrote a long letter.

examples.text: الرسام كتب الملاحظات بالحبر الأسود عالهامش.
examples.trans: The illustrator wrote the notes in black ink in the margin.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Also used in the mild Jordanian exclamation يا لطيف! ('goodness gracious!').

examples.trans: Hot bread makes people pleasant!
Goodness gracious, the suitcase is so heavy!

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Conditional particle used for hypothetical or impossible situations (contrary-to-fact conditions).

examples.text: لو بعرف إنك جاي، كنت استنيتك.
examples.trans: If I knew you were coming, I would have waited for you.

examples.text: لو لقينا المفتاح بدري كنا فتحنا الصندوق امبارح.
examples.trans: If we had found the key earlier we would have opened the chest yesterday.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: I went to Petra one time.

examples.text: جربنا الوصفة مرة تانية بس بخففنا السكر شوي.
examples.trans: We tried the recipe one more time, though we reduced the sugar slightly.

meanings.note: Feminine Arabic word meaning 'double' or 'twofold', agreeing with رنة.

examples.text: الجرس رنّ رنة مزدوجة قبل ما يفتحوا الباب.
examples.trans: The bell gave a double ring before they opened the door.

examples.text: الشبابيك الجديدة لها زجاج مزدوج لعزل الصوت والبرد.
examples.trans: The new windows have double-pane glass to insulate against noise and cold.

meanings.note: Form X passive participle of استعمل (to use); standard label for second-hand books, furniture, or gear.

examples.text: لقينا هادا الدفتر النادر بمحل كتب مستعملة.
examples.trans: We found this rare notebook in a second-hand bookshop.

examples.text: العلبة مبينة مستعملة بس نظيفة ومرتبة.
examples.trans: The tin looks used, yet it is clean and neat.

meanings.note: Feminine participle from طبع ('to print'), agreeing with قائمة ('menu').

examples.text: القائمة المطبوعة الجديدة عليها كل أسعار المشروبات.
examples.trans: The new printed menu has all the drink prices on it.

examples.text: معي نسخة مطبوعة من العقد عشان نراجعها سوا.
examples.trans: I have a printed copy of the contract so we can review it together.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Refers to a paper envelope used for letters or documents.

examples.trans: I put the money in an envelope.

examples.text: حطينا البطاقات كلها جوا مغلف ورق بني.
examples.trans: We put all the cards inside a brown paper envelope.

meanings.note: Used for both a workplace (office) and the piece of furniture (desk).

examples.trans: I am waiting for you in my office.

examples.text: لقينا الخريطة التانية جوا درج مكتب جدي.
examples.trans: We found the second map inside my grandfather's desk drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مكتبات.

examples.trans: There are old bookshops in downtown Amman.
The public library is a quiet place to read.

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: The name is written on the board.

examples.text: الرقم مكتوب بخط صغير تحت الختم الأحمر.
examples.trans: The number is written in small handwriting beneath the red seal.

meanings.note: Used for remarks, annotations, or paying attention to details.

examples.trans: I have a small note on the work.

examples.text: سجلنا ملاحظة صغيرة عن نكهة قشر البرتقال.
examples.trans: We jotted down a short note about the orange peel flavour.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مواعيد.

examples.trans: I always appreciate punctuality.

examples.text: عندنا موعد مهم يوم الجمعة الظهر.
examples.trans: We have an important appointment Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who rang the bell?

examples.text: مين كتب هاي الملاحظة عالورقة بالحبر الأزرق؟
examples.trans: Who wrote this note on the paper in blue ink?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نازلة, plural: نازلين).

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs for breakfast.

examples.text: مش مصدق إنك نازلة بنفس النزل!
examples.trans: I cannot believe you are staying at the same inn!

meanings.note: Can refer to objects lacking moisture or metaphorically to a rude or blunt person.

examples.trans: The bread is dry, it can't be eaten.

examples.text: لازم نمسح الصحن بمنديل ناشف قبل ما نحط الكيكة.
examples.trans: We must wipe the plate with a dry cloth before putting the cake on.

meanings.note: Instrument noun from نشّف (to dry); denotes blotting paper for wet ink as well as a clothes dryer.

examples.text: استعملوا ورقة النشافة عشان ما يلطخ الحبر.
examples.trans: Use the blotting paper so the ink does not smudge.

examples.text: حطينا الغسيل بالنشافة عشان ينشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: We put the laundry in the dryer so it dries quickly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian pronunciation (often نعنع in rapid speech) for fresh or dried mint added to tea.

examples.text: قطفنا شوية نعناع أخضر عشان الشاي.
examples.trans: We picked some fresh mint for the tea.
The dried mint in the jar has a strong aroma.

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'the same' when followed by a noun, or as a reflexive.

examples.trans: We live in the same building.

examples.text: استعملنا نفس الوصفة بس زدنا شوية برش برتقال.
examples.trans: We used the exact same recipe, though we added a little orange zest.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: This boy is very smart.

examples.text: هاد المحل ببيع أطيب كنافة نابلسية بعمان.
examples.trans: This shop sells the best Nabulsi kunafa in Amman.

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine demonstrative adverb parallel to هناك (over there).

examples.text: اللوحة القديمة معلقة هنيك عند الدرج.
examples.trans: The old painting is hanging over there by the stairs.

examples.text: روحوا هنيك تحت شجرة الزيزفون الجو أبرد.
examples.trans: Go over there under the linden tree; it is cooler.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: There is someone asking about you.

examples.text: اشتريت كتاب واحد بس من المعرض لأنه كان غالي.
examples.trans: I bought just one book from the fair because it was expensive.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Used for a person or thing falling down.

examples.trans: Be careful the boy doesn't fall.

examples.text: لا تحط الصحن عالحفة عشان ما يوقع وينكسر.
examples.trans: Don't put the plate right on the edge so it doesn't fall and break.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today is a long day.

examples.text: سافرنا عالعقبة وقعدنا هناك يوم كامل عالشط.
examples.trans: We traveled to Aqaba and spent a whole day there at the beach.
